unified_features.name: Book library
unified_features.rationale: Only Shelfie has a library feature (Readr has a books table but no code using it). Readr's Book (title only) is a subset of Shelfie's Book (title, author), so one Book entity serves both.
unified_features.behaviour: A signed-in person adds a book (title required, author optional), lists their books, edits and removes them. Each person sees only their own library.
unified_features.improvements: Shelfie can only list books already in the database; add create, edit and delete, validate title on the server, and scope books to their owner.

unified_features.name: Star ratings
unified_features.rationale: Shelfie and Readr rate identically (integer 1-5 stars, appended). Shelfie's version is kept because it also has an API and a database CHECK; Readr's (M03) is dropped as a duplicate. The 1-10 'score' scale in Shelfie's README and spec is contradicted by its code and is not used.
unified_features.behaviour: A person rates one of their books with an integer 1-5 ('stars'); rating again replaces their earlier rating; anything else is rejected with 400 and an error message; the rating can be cleared.
unified_features.improvements: Both sources append a new row per rating; the unified app keeps one rating per person per book (unique key, upsert). Range enforced on the server and by a database CHECK.

unified_features.name: Library export (JSON)
unified_features.rationale: Only Shelfie exports. The code exports JSON; the README and spec promise CSV, which does not exist and is not built (the user said to trust what the apps do).
unified_features.behaviour: GET export returns a JSON array of {title, stars} for the signed-in person's books, one entry per book, stars null when unrated.
unified_features.improvements: Scoped to the owner; one entry per book (follows from U02's one rating per person per book).

unified_features.name: Reading lists
unified_features.rationale: Only Readr has reading lists, and the user asked for them. Readr implements only adding a book to a list; the rest of the lifecycle exists only as tables.
unified_features.behaviour: A person creates a named list, renames and deletes it, adds their own books to it and removes them, and views each list with its books. A book can be on many lists, once per list.
unified_features.improvements: Add create, view, rename, delete and remove-book operations (absent in Readr); unique (list, book) pair; reject unknown or other people's list or book ids; lists belong to one person.
